findings.description: RULES.md rule 3 requires a behaviour change to ship with a test in the same directory named <Module>.test.ts. The plan changes behaviour in two modules (new src/http/RateLimiter.ts and modified src/http/handler.ts: new third parameter, new pre-routing 429 path, anonymous bucketing) but proposes only src/http/RateLimiter.test.ts. Plan tests 5 and 6 exercise createApp, i.e. handler.ts behaviour, from a file named after a different module; they belong in src/http/handler.test.ts.

The plan's 'unbounded-growth guard' does not bound growth in the case that matters. It sweeps only entries whose window has already expired; a client rotating x-client-id on every request (the key is a caller-supplied header) produces only live, unexpired entries, so nothing is reclaimed, the map grows past maxTrackedClients without limit, and every insert past the cap triggers an O(n) scan that reclaims nothing, so per-request CPU grows with the attack. That is a worse resource-starvation vector than the one T-4 fixes. Needs a hard cap (eviction by oldest window, or refuse-to-track once full) or an explicit argued out-of-scope statement.

Plan test 4 ('a denied request does not extend the window') does not discriminate as described: if the stub clock is not advanced between the calls that exhaust the limit and the denied calls, windowStart and the denial timestamp are identical, so advancing just past the original windowMs admits the client whether or not a denial reset windowStart. The test must advance the clock strictly inside the window before the denied calls.

Plan test 5 asserts the warn line's requestId is the refused request's id, but handler.ts falls back to randomUUID() when x-request-id is absent, so the refused request must explicitly carry an x-request-id header. Also the first (202) request logs 'report queued', so the shared sink holds two lines; the assertion must select the warn/'rate limited' line rather than copying router.test.ts's lines[0] pattern.

Bucketing all header-less traffic under one shared 'anonymous' key closes the bypass but reintroduces the ticket's own failure mode inside that bucket: one flooding header-less client starves every other header-less client. The plan should state this residual rather than presenting the shared bucket as strictly safer.

IncomingRequest.headers is a plain Record<string, string | undefined> with no normalisation, so a caller passing X-Client-Id silently lands in the anonymous bucket. For the request id that was cosmetic; for a limiter it is a bypass. A case-insensitive lookup helper stays within Node built-ins.

The stated justification 'a denied request does not increment the count, so a client hammering a closed window cannot push its own reset time out' is unsound for a fixed window: reset time is windowStart + windowMs, independent of count. The behaviour is correct; the reason given is not the reason.

The plan's 'npx tsc --noEmit' verification step would fetch TypeScript, which the repo declares nowhere (no dependencies or devDependencies); it is not runnable offline and sits awkwardly beside rule 2. npm test (node --test) is the only verification the repo supports.

Running the limiter strictly in front of routing means GET /health probes and unmatched 404 paths consume a client's quota. Defensible, but it is an unmentioned behaviour change with no test; one sentence deciding it deliberately would close it.

report.notes: Agent code review, round 1, as instructed. Reviewer read the full 348-line diff, the approved plan, ran npm test (15/15), probed the limiter's edge cases with a scratch script, and type-checked with an external tsc 5.9.3 + @types/node.

findings.description: The anonymous bucket and 'every request counts, including /health' are each justified separately but their interaction is an availability hazard the tests lock in. All requests with no x-client-id share the key 'anonymous', and the limiter runs before routing, so a load-balancer or k8s probe hitting GET /health (which carries no x-client-id) draws from the same default 100/min window as every other header-less caller. Scenario: a burst of 100 anonymous requests exhausts 'anonymous'; the next /health probe gets 429, the LB pulls the instance from rotation, load shifts to peers which trip the same bucket. A quota event becomes an outage. The plan's justification ('a caller that polls /health hard enough to exhaust its own window is a caller the limiter should be refusing') is false under the shared bucket: the probe's quota is spent by other clients, not by the probe.

handler.test.ts asserts an exact retryAfterSeconds of 60 twice while the app runs on the real Date.now (the injectable clock is not injected there). retryAfterSeconds is Math.ceil((windowStart + 60000 - now) / 1000), so it is 60 only while both app.handle calls land in the same 1000ms; a GC pause or loaded CI yields 59 and fails. It is also the ONLY assertion pinning the retryAfterSeconds arithmetic at all: the deterministic tests only check > 0, which Math.max(1, ...) makes true for almost any arithmetic mistake.

The diff changes x-request-id resolution from an exact lowercase lookup to the case-insensitive helper. That is a real behaviour change on the request-id path governed by ruling r-eftp2zdb6as643np (a caller sending X-Request-Id previously got a fresh randomUUID and now gets its own id honoured), and no test in the diff covers it. RULES.md rule 3 requires a behaviour change to ship with a test.

header() returns on the first name-matching key even when that key's value is undefined, and IncomingRequest.headers is explicitly Record<string, string | undefined>, so undefined values are in contract. With headers { 'X-Client-Id': undefined, 'x-client-id': 'c1' } the helper returns undefined and the request is bucketed as anonymous despite carrying a real client id. The same shape on x-request-id drops the caller's id for a randomUUID, losing the correlation the ruling is about.

maxTrackedClients is not validated and the guard degrades quietly on non-positive-integer input. Verified by running the module: NaN leaves the map UNBOUNDED (NaN >= NaN is false, so eviction never fires; 500 rotating ids produced 500 entries), which defeats the cap entirely; 2.5 settles at 3 entries; 0 and -1 still track 1 client. A misconfigured maxTrackedClients: Number(process.env.X) with an unset var is exactly the NaN case. The ordering invariant itself was traced and confirmed sound on every path.

A whitespace-only or empty x-request-id makes handle() reject instead of responding: header(...) ?? randomUUID() does not treat '' or '   ' as absent, and AppLogger.withRequestId throws on a blank id. Pre-existing on the router path, but this diff adds a second call site for it on the new 429 path and rewrites the request-id resolution line anyway.

RateLimitDecision.resetAt is never asserted by any test and is unused by the handler, so a wrong resetAt (e.g. computed from now rather than windowStart, silently turning the fixed window into a sliding one for reporting) would be caught only indirectly via the flaky exact-60 assertion.

Two benign divergences from the approved plan. (1) RateLimitDecision gains a limit field the plan's interface sketch omits; it is required by the plan's own log-line spec, so the addition is right and the sketch was incomplete. (2) The plan's Verification section asserts the repo has no type checking at all and that tsc is unrunnable offline, but the repo does check in a tsconfig.json with strict: true, which the plan never mentions; the new code type-checks clean under tsc 5.9.3 with @types/node. Nothing is broken, but the plan's stated reason for skipping the step rests on a false premise about the repo.

# Session handover -- T-4, per-client rate limiting

Targeted autonomous session (`/story auto T-4`). One item, completed and committed as `9b5c4a0`.

## What shipped

**T-4: Add per-client rate limiting to the HTTP handler** -- complete.

- **New `src/http/RateLimiter.ts`**: fixed window per client id, injected clock, and a *hard* cap on tracked clients enforced by O(1) oldest-window eviction. Constructor validates `limit`/`windowMs`/`maxTrackedClients` as positive integers.
- **`src/http/handler.ts`**: limiter runs in front of routing; 429 with `{ error, retryAfterSeconds }`; headers matched case-insensitively; missing client id shares one `"anonymous"` bucket; refusal logged through `AppLogger` under the request id.
- **Tests**: `src/http/RateLimiter.test.ts` and `src/http/handler.test.ts` (rule 3 -- the change touches two modules, so it ships two test files). Suite 22/22.

## Decisions worth carrying forward

1. **`GET /health` is exempt from the limiter; unmatched paths are not.** This reversed the approved plan after code review round 1. A probe sends no `x-client-id`, so it lands in the shared `"anonymous"` bucket and its quota is spent by unrelated header-less callers: a burst 429s the probe, the LB pulls the instance from rotation, load shifts to peers that trip the same bucket. A rate limiter must not be able to take the service out of rotation. The exemption is scoped to method *and* path, and `POST /health` is metered like anything else. Cost accepted and recorded in the plan: `/health` is now the one path whose log volume has no ceiling.

2. **The cap is a hard cap, not a sweep of expired entries.** The key is a caller-supplied header, so a client rotating `x-client-id` every request produces only *live* entries; an expiry sweep would reclaim nothing while charging a scan for it, making per-request CPU rise with the flood. Eviction takes the oldest window in O(1) by keeping `Map` insertion order equal to `windowStart` ascending (a reset deletes and re-inserts the entry).

3. **Eviction's cost is real and was taken deliberately.** Under a sustained rotating-id flood the oldest entry is a *legitimate* client, so enforcement is effectively suspended for real clients for the duration. The fix for that is identity the caller cannot mint -- authentication -- not a cleverer eviction order. Explicitly out of scope for T-4.

4. **Options are validated at construction.** `maxTrackedClients: NaN` would make `size >= max` false forever and silently leave the map unbounded -- the exact failure the cap exists to prevent. `Number(process.env.X)` with an unset variable is that case.

5. **The repo has a `tsconfig.json` with `strict: true` but no compiler installed** (no deps/devDeps), and Node strips types without checking them. So `npm test` is the whole in-repo verification story and a type-level mistake is caught by nothing. Pre-existing; this change accepts it. Code review type-checked the new code out-of-band and found it clean.

## Process notes

- **The codex review bridge is not available on this harness** -- no `review_plan` tool is registered, so both plan review and code review ran on the agent fallback per the guide's instruction. Worth knowing before assuming a codex-backed review ran.
- Review was productive rather than ceremonial: plan review caught an unbounded-memory hole in the first draft's "growth guard", and code review round 1 caught the `/health` availability hazard, which the tests at that point had locked in as intended behaviour. Round 2 mutation-tested each claimed fix (reverting the implementation line and re-running) before approving -- that is what distinguished genuine fixes from restatements, and it also surfaced three tests that passed vacuously.

## Incidental fix

A blank or whitespace-only `x-request-id` previously threw out of `AppLogger.withRequestId` instead of responding. Pre-existing, but this diff rewrote that exact line and added a second call site for it, so it was fixed inline (`?.trim() || randomUUID()`) with a test rather than filed.

## What's next

Nothing is blocked and nothing was left half-done. No issues were filed this session. The backlog is unchanged apart from T-4 moving to complete -- run `/story` for the current ranking.
